desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} On August 15, 1974, marking the 29th anniversary of Korea's liberation, the country's first subway line, the 'Jongno Line,' opened. Since then, Seoulites have lived in the “Subway Age” for five decades. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway is familiar to everyone who has traveled to and from Seoul. It was not just a convenient public transportation system that eases commutes to school and work; it was a vehicle for a ‘new era of modern life.’ Back then, the subway was a new experience for everyone in Seoul. Over time, as we adapted to this new era, the subway gradually changed our mindset, lifestyle, culture, and the city itself. It has served as a commuter train for the city’s many workers, a transportation service that makes it easy for everyone to get around and keep appointments, a meet-up point, and a venue for consumption. The subway also provided a social space where people could mingle, fostering both a sense of community and deep aloneness. Furthermore, it has reshaped urban spaces and living areas, and as a comfortable cultural space accessible anywhere, it has expanded people's cultural enjoyment. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway has been “connecting” Seoul through its underground network and to the outlying areas, shaping the capital city as we know it today. To mark the 50th anniversary of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway, the Seoul Museum of History and Seoul Metro have partnered to present this commemorative exhibition. We cordially invite you to this exhibition, which we hope will offer an opportunity to reflect on Seoul’s story, created by the subway and its people, and to envision what the future holds for the city.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 1974年8月15日、光復29周年を記念する日、韓国初の地下鉄「チョンノ(鐘路)線」が開通しました。それから50年にわたって、私たちは地下鉄の時代を歩んできました。ソウルを行き来する誰もが利用してきたソウルの地下鉄は、学校や職場へとスムーズに移動できる便利な交通手段であるだけでなく、「現代生活の新しい時代」を切り開く役割を果たしてきました。地下鉄は、私たちにとって初めての体験であり、新しい時代の経験を共有する中で、意識や生活様式、文化、そして都市の姿を徐々に変えてきました。地下鉄は都市の労働者を運ぶ通勤電車であり、誰もが簡単に移動し、約束の時間を守ることができる交通手段であり、出会いの場所や消費の場でもありました。それは、社会的な交流がありながら孤独も感じさせる場所でもありました。また、都市空間と生活圏を新しく再編成し、どこでも快適に文化に接することができる空間として、人々の文化的享受を広げました。 このように、地下鉄は地下の世界を通じて、または都市の外縁とつながりながら、ソウルを大きく「連結」させ、今日のソウルを作り上げてきました。ソウル地下鉄開通50周年を記念して、ソウル歴史博物館とソウルメトロは共同で展示を開催します。この展示にご参加いただき、過去50年間にわたって地下鉄と人々が共に作り上げてきたソウルの物語を振り返り、未来の姿を描く貴重な機会となることを願っています。
desc_l10n.ko: 1974년 8월 15일 광복 29주년을 기념하는 날, 우리나라 최초의 지하철 '종로선'이 개통되었고, 그로부터 우리는 50년에 이르는 지하철 시대를 살아오고 있습니다. 서울을 오가는 사람이면 누구나 타봤을 서울 지하철은 우리를 정체 없이 학교와 직장으로 날라주는 편리한 대중교통수단임을 넘어서 '현대 생활의 새로운 시대'를 열어간 매개체였습니다. 우리 모두에게 처음이었던 지하철은 새 시대에 대한 경험을 함께 쌓으며 우리의 의식과 생활·문화 양식, 도시 모습을 서서히 바꿔나갔습니다. 지하철은 도시 노동자들을 실어 나르는 통근열차이자 누구나 쉽게 이동하고 약속시간을 지킬 수 있게 한 교통수단이었으며, 만남의 장소이자 소비공간이었습니다. 사람들이 부대끼는 사회적 공간으로 공동체 의식과 동시에 외로움을 키워간 곳이기도 했습니다. 나아가 도시공간과 생활권을 새롭게 재편하였으며, 어디서나 접할 수 있는 쾌적한 문화공간으로 사람들의 문화 향유를 확대하였습니다. 이처럼 지하철은 땅속 세계를 통해 지하로, 또는 도시 외곽으로 거대하게 서울을 '연결'하며 오늘의 서울을 만들어 왔습니다. 서울 지하철 개통 50주년을 기념하여 서울역사박물관과 서울교통공사는 공동으로 전시를 개최합니다. 전시에 함께 하시어 지난 반세기 동안 지하철과 사람들이 함께 만들어온 서울의 이야기를 되돌아보고, 다시 내일의 모습을 그려보는 소중한 기회가 되기를 바랍니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 1974年8月15日，值此光复29周年之际，韩国首条地铁‘钟路线’正式开通，自那时起我们已经进入地铁时代长达50年。无论是谁，只要是往返于首尔的人，肯定都乘坐过首尔地铁。首尔地铁不仅是一种便利的大众交通工具，能够不堵车地将我们送到学校和工作场所，还成为开启‘现代生活新时代’的媒介。对我们所有人来说，第一次体验地铁的时刻，也是在共同积累对新时代的体验，同时地铁也逐渐改变了我们的意识、生活文化模式以及城市的面貌。地铁不仅是运送城市劳动者的通勤列车，让任何人都能够轻松出行、准时赴约的交通工具，它还是一个见面地点和消费空间。地铁作为一个人们相互接触的社会空间，在培育社区意识的同时，也增添了些许孤独感。地铁进一步重新规划了城市空间和生活圈，并通过随处可见的宜人文化空间，扩大了人们的文化享受。 地铁通过地下世界、或者延伸至城市边缘的大规模‘连接’，塑造了今天的首尔。为了纪念首尔地铁开通50周年，首尔历史博物馆和首尔交通公社联合举办了此次展览。希望大家能够参与其中，回顾过去半个世纪以来地铁与人们共同书写的首尔故事，并借此机会描绘明日的蓝图。

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} On August 15, 1974, marking the 29th anniversary of Korea's liberation, the country's first subway line, the 'Jongno Line,' opened. Since then, Seoulites have lived in the “Subway Age” for five decades. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway is familiar to everyone who has traveled to and from Seoul. It was not just a convenient public transportation system that eases commutes to school and work; it was a vehicle for a ‘new era of modern life.’ Back then, the subway was a new experience for everyone in Seoul. Over time, as we adapted to this new era, the subway gradually changed our mindset, lifestyle, culture, and the city itself. It has served as a commuter train for the city’s many workers, a transportation service that makes it easy for everyone to get around and keep appointments, a meet-up point, and a venue for consumption. The subway also provided a social space where people could mingle, fostering both a sense of community and deep aloneness. Furthermore, it has reshaped urban spaces and living areas, and as a comfortable cultural space accessible anywhere, it has expanded people's cultural enjoyment. The Seoul Metropolitan Subway has been “connecting” Seoul through its underground network and to the outlying areas, shaping the capital city as we know it today. To mark the 50th anniversary of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway, the Seoul Museum of History and Seoul Metro have partnered to present this commemorative exhibition. We cordially invite you to this exhibition, which we hope will offer an opportunity to reflect on Seoul’s story, created by the subway and its people, and to envision what the future holds for the city.
name: 50th Anniversary of Seoul Metropolitan Subway <Subway in Seoul>

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Looking at nature closely resembles looking into one's own inner self. Park Kyung-mook's work contains the journey of reaching the silence of muk (默) through the material of meok (墨, ink). The traces of ink accumulated and permeated on the canvas are an accumulation of time and a process of thought, and the shapes resembling black rocks and islands, rather than explaining or defining something, allow the viewer to pause for a moment and observe their own mind. The path to Simwon (心源), the root of the mind where all thoughts begin, is not far away. Through the act of letting one's gaze linger along the deep empty spaces created by the ink, and quietly observing the vitality of trees that embrace a long period of time, we naturally confront our inner selves. The deep ink, the empty spaces, and the trees holding time form a single garden within the space. Rather than a real garden, it is a landscape of thought unfolding in the mind, and a place where one can stay for a while, catch their breath, and listen to the source of their inner self. The Garden of Simwon: Ink and Silence is a place where thoughts built up with ink and landscapes formed by time meet. Walking through the garden of Simwon, we hope it will be a time to face the tranquil landscape existing in each person's mind.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 自然を見つめることは、結局のところ、自らの内面を見つめることにほかなりません。パク・ギョンムクの作品は、「墨」という素材を通して、「黙」へと至る精神の旅を描いています。画面に幾重にも重なり、静かに染み込んだ墨の痕跡は、時間の積み重ねであり、思索の軌跡でもあります。黒い岩や島を思わせる造形は、何かを説明したり定義したりするのではなく、鑑賞者に立ち止まり、自らの心と静かに向き合うひとときをもたらします。「心源」――すべての思索が始まる心の源へと至る道は、決して遠くにはありません。墨が生み出す深い余白に目を留め、長い歳月を刻んだ木々の生命力を静かに見つめること。その時間の中で、私たちは自然と自らの内面に出会います。深い墨の色彩、豊かな余白、そして時を宿した木々が、一つの空間の中で一つの庭を形づくります。それは現実の庭ではなく、心の中に広がる思索の風景であり、しばし足を止め、呼吸を整え、自らの心の源に耳を澄ませるための場所です。〈心源の庭：墨と黙〉は、墨が積み重ねてきた思索と、時間が育んだ風景とが出会う場です。「心源の庭」を歩きながら、それぞれの心の中に息づく静かな風景と向き合うひとときをお過ごしください。
desc_l10n.ko: 자연을 바라보는 일은 결국 자신의 내면을 들여다보는 일과 닮아 있습니다. 박경묵의 작업은 먹(墨)이라는 재료를 통해 침묵의 묵(默)에 이르는 여정을 담고 있습니다. 화면 위에 쌓이고 스며든 먹의 흔적은 시간의 축적이자 사유의 과정이며, 검은 바위와 섬을 닮은 형상들은 무엇을 설명하거나 규정하기보다, 관람자로 하여금 잠시 멈추어 서서 스스로의 마음을 바라보게 합니다. 심원(心源), 즉 모든 사유가 시작되는 마음의 근원에 이르는 길은 멀리 있지 않습니다. 먹이 만들어낸 깊은 여백을 따라 시선을 머무르게 하는 일, 오랜 시간을 품은 나무의 생명력을 가만히 바라보는 일 속에서 우리는 자연스럽게 자신의 내면과 마주하게 됩니다. 깊은 먹과 여백, 그리고 시간을 품은 나무가 공간 안에서 하나의 정원을 이룹니다. 그것은 실제의 정원이기보다 마음속에 펼쳐지는 사유의 풍경이며, 잠시 머물러 자신의 호흡을 가다듬고 내면의 근원에 귀 기울일 수 있는 장소입니다. 〈心源의 정원 : 먹과 묵〉은 먹으로 쌓아 올린 사유와 시간으로 빚어낸 풍경이 만나는 자리입니다. 심원의 정원을 거닐며, 각자의 마음속에 존재하는 고요한 풍경과 마주하는 시간이 되기를 바랍니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 凝望自然这件事，终究与审视自身内心别无二致。朴京默的创作，通过“墨”这一媒介，铺展开一条通往沉静之“默”的修行之路。在画面层层晕染、渗透的墨痕，是时光沉淀，亦是思索流转。那些酷似黑石、孤岛的意象，无意定义、解说任何事物，只为让观者驻足停顿，反观自我本心。心源，即，一切思绪生发的心灵本源，通往它的道路并不遥远。当目光流连于墨色铺展的悠远留白，静静凝视饱经岁月沉淀的林木生机，我们便自然而然地与内在自我相逢。浓墨、留白，承载漫长时光的林木，在空间之中构筑成一方庭院。这并非实体园林，而是心底铺展的思索之境；一处可供暂歇、调匀呼吸、聆听内心本源的栖心之地。《心源之庭：墨和默》是墨色堆叠出的哲思，与时光铸就的景致相融相会之所。愿您漫步心源之庭，拥有一段与心底那份静谧光景相逢的时光。

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《 Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh 》 is a two-person exhibition featuring Camille Norment and Min Oh that sheds new light on what is commonly referred to as "noise," including irregular sounds, unpredictable variables, and elements pushed outside the boundaries of established systems. Noise is recontextualized not as an obstruction to be eliminated, but as a fertile ground where new relationships and meanings emerge. Camille Norment and Min Oh respond to this inquiry through their respective creative methodologies. Min Oh presents her time-based installation series, Simultaneous, displayed together in one place for the first time—a body of work researched and produced over several years as part of the Arko Multi-disciplinary Arts Support Project. Concurrently, Camille Norment marks her inaugural solo presentation at a domestic museum with Plexus (Rhizome) Seoul, a sound installation commissioned specifically by the Arko Art Center.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《ズレゆく波動、揺らぐ時間》は、私たちが普段「ノイズ」と呼ぶもの —— 不規則な音、予測不可能な変数、システムの外へと追いやられたものたち —— を新たな視点で見つめ直す、オ・ミンとカミーユ・ノーメントによる二人展です。ノイズとは排除すべき障害物ではなく、むしろその内部から新しい関係性や意味が生まれる場所であるかもしれません。オ・ミンとカミーユ・ノーメントは、それぞれの方法でこの問いに答えています。オ・ミンは、アルコ多次元芸術創作主体支援事業の一環として数年間にわたり研究・制作してきた、時間を基盤とするインスタレーション〈同時〉連作を初めて一ヶ所に展示します。また、韓国の美術館では初の展示となるカミーユ・ノーメントは、アルコ美術館のコミッション作品であるサウンド・インスタレーション〈プレクサス(リゾーム)ソウル〉を披露します。
desc_l10n.ko: 《어긋난 파동, 흔들리는 시간》은 우리가 흔히 '노이즈'라고 부르는 것 — 불규칙한 소리, 예측할 수 없는 변수, 시스템 밖으로 밀려난 것들 — 을 새롭게 바라보는 오민과 카밀 노먼트의 2인전입니다. 노이즈는 제거해야 할 방해물이 아니라, 오히려 그 안에서 새로운 관계와 의미가 태어나는 장소일 수 있습니다. 오민과 카밀 노먼트는 각자의 방식으로 이 질문에 답합니다. 오민은 아르코 다원예술 창작주체 지원사업의 일환으로 수년간 연구, 제작해 온 시간 기반 설치 〈동시〉 연작을 처음으로 한자리에서 보여주며, 국내 미술관 최초로 전시하는 카밀 노먼트는 사운드 설치 작품인 〈플렉서스(리좀) 서울〉을 아르코미술관의 커미션으로 선보입니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《错位波动，摇曳时光》是吴敏与Camille Norment的双人展，展览用全新视角审视我们口中的 “噪声”—— 无序的声响、不可预判的变数、被体系排挤在外的存在。噪声并非是必须清除的干扰物，反而可能是催生全新关联与意义的载体。两位艺术家用各自的创作方式诠释这一理念。吴敏带来其依托ARKO多元艺术创作扶持项目、历经数年研究打造的时间装置系列作品《同时》，该系列首次完整集中展出。Camille Norment则携声音装置作品《交织网络（rhyzome）・首尔》亮相，这件作品为ARKO美术馆委任创作，也是该作品首次在韩国国内美术馆公开展出。

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《 Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh 》 is a two-person exhibition featuring Camille Norment and Min Oh that sheds new light on what is commonly referred to as "noise," including irregular sounds, unpredictable variables, and elements pushed outside the boundaries of established systems. Noise is recontextualized not as an obstruction to be eliminated, but as a fertile ground where new relationships and meanings emerge. Camille Norment and Min Oh respond to this inquiry through their respective creative methodologies. Min Oh presents her time-based installation series, Simultaneous, displayed together in one place for the first time—a body of work researched and produced over several years as part of the Arko Multi-disciplinary Arts Support Project. Concurrently, Camille Norment marks her inaugural solo presentation at a domestic museum with Plexus (Rhizome) Seoul, a sound installation commissioned specifically by the Arko Art Center.
name: Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh

Under the theme “Extreme Design Experience: From Street to Gallery,” the program will offer enthusiasts a sensory journey. As part of the seasonal DDP Special Tour series, this autumn’s program contrasts “Touchable Design vs. Collectible Design,” ranging from hands-on, experiential design objects to unique collectible pieces expressing value, meaning, story, and identity.

desc_l10n.ko: 서울디자인재단은 '디자인&아트' 전시와 연계한 DDP 가을 스페셜투어를 운영합니다. '디자인 체험 극과 극 : 거리에서 갤러리까지'라는 주제로 애호가에게 감각적 경험을 선사할 예정입니다. 계절별 맟춤형 투어 콘텐츠로 자리 잡은 <DDP 스페셜투어>의 이번 가을 시즌은 '터처블 디자인 vs 콜렉터블 디자인'으로 직접 만지고 느껴보는 체험 중심의 디자인 오브제에서부터 가치∙의미∙스토리∙정체성의 표현을 담은 소장하고 싶은 단 하나의 오브제까지 상반된 디자인 세계를 표현합니다.

In particular, the exhibited works of Van Gogh are part of the 'Masterpiece Original Series,' a simulacrum created using patented 3D UV printing technology. This technology recreates Van Gogh's brushstrokes and colors, allowing visitors to feel the texture of the original works at their fingertips.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 今回の展示ではゴッホの作品を単に視覚的に鑑賞するだけでなく、来場者が作品の質感に直接触れることで、ゴッホの芸術をより深く味わえます。 特に展示されるゴッホの作品は、特許取得済みの3D UVプリンターを活用し、ゴッホの筆遣いや色彩を再現したシミュラークル『マスターピース・オリジナルシリーズ』で、来場者が原作を再現した質感を指先で感じられるようになっています。
desc_l10n.ko: 이번 전시는 고흐의 작품을 단순히 시각적으로만 감상하는 것이 아니라, 관람객들이 작품의 질감을 직접 만져보며 고흐의 예술을 보다 깊게 체험할 수 있는 기회를 제공한다. 특히, 전시된 고흐의 작품들은 특허 받은 3D UV프린팅 기술을 활용해 고흐의 붓터치와 색감을 재현한 시뮬라크 ‘마스터피스 오리지널 시리즈'로 관람객들이 실제 원작을 재현한 질감을 손끝으로 느낄 수 있게 된다.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} As the season deepens, leaves gradually change color, fruits ripen fully, and nature meets its moment of fruition. Aechae’s autumn exhibition Chubun: The Beginning of Autumn resembles this seasonal flow. Just as a single tree takes root over time, blossoms, and eventually bears fruit, may you enjoy the maturity and abundance of this season before Chuseok, achieving stronger results and generous accomplishments in your own place.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 秋が深まるこの時間、葉は徐々に色づき、実はたくさん実り、自然はその結実の瞬間を迎えます。エチェの秋展<秋分：秋の始まり>は、そのような季節の流れに似ています。一本の木が長い時間をかけて根を下ろし、花を咲かせ、そして実を結ぶように、秋夕を控えたこの季節の成熟と豊かさを楽しみ、各自の場でより良い成果が得られることを願います。
desc_l10n.ko: 가을이 깊어지는 이 시간, 잎은 서서히 물들고, 열매는 알차게 맺히며, 자연은 그 결실의 순간을 맞이합니다. 애채의 가을전 <추분 : 가을의 시작>은 그러한 계절의 흐름을 닮아 있습니다. 한 그루의 나무가 오랜 시간 뿌리를 내리고 꽃을 피워 결국 열매를 맺듯, 추석을 앞둔 이 계절의 성숙과 풍요를 즐기며, 각자의 자리에서 더욱 단단한 결실과 넉넉한 성취를 이루시길 바랍니다.

Aechae’s autumn exhibition Chubun: The Beginning of Autumn resembles this seasonal flow. Just as a single tree takes root over time, blossoms, and eventually bears fruit, may you enjoy the maturity and abundance of this season before Chuseok, achieving stronger results and generous accomplishments in your own place.
name: Chubun: The Beginning of Autumn

desc_l10n.ko: 이머시브 시어터의 선구자인 영국 제작사 '펀치드렁크'의 작품으로, 셰익스피어의 비극 ‘맥베스’를 감각적이고 영화적으로 재해석한 몰입형 공연입니다. 전 세계 공연계에 새로운 패러다임을 선사한 히트작, 퍼포머와 직접 마주하고 호흡하며 오감으로 느끼는 최고의 경험을 해보세요.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} What was your childhood like? This exhibition begins with that question. The international exchange exhibition, “Stories of Children Who Lived Through the War: Childhood under the Siege,” aims to convey the preciousness of peace through 38 stories of children who endured the longest siege in modern history, which took place in Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia, from 1992 to 1995. For 1,425 days, children in Sarajevo lived isolated from the world, experiencing a different daily life than ordinary children. Their lives, filled with the pain of war and the preciousness of everyday moments, are told with quiet resilience. These deeply personal stories are not just about Sarajevo, a city 8,465 kilometers away from Seoul. They are stories of families, friends, and neighbors, resonating deeply with the audience. Through this exhibition, the hope is for you to feel that "people are strong, and children are strong!"
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} あなたの子供の頃はどうでしたか？今回の展示はこの質問から始まります。 国際交流展『戦争を経験した子供たちの話: Childhood under the Siege』は、ボスニアの首都サラエボで起きた現代史上最も長い包囲戦(1992-1995)を経験した子供たちの38の話を通じて平和の大切さを伝えます。1,425日間、世の中と断絶した都市の中で平凡な子供たちとは違う日常を過ごしたサラエボの子供たちの人生は、戦争の苦痛と日常の大切さを淡々と解きほぐします。これらの話は、ソウルから8,465km離れた都市サラエボだけの話ではありません。私の家族、私の友人の話でもあり、私の隣人の話として観覧客に強い衝撃を与えるでしょう。今回の展示を通して「人は強い。 そして子供たちは強い！」というメッセージを感じてください。

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Superior Gallery has organized an exhibition titled 'Super Moon on My Hand: Moon Jar' featuring the artists Kang Min-sung, Kim Kyung-hee, and Jo Sung-hyun, who are furthering the tradition while evolving it into contemporary lifestyle art. Showcasing works that reinterpret traditional techniques and imagery in a modern way, these pieces fuse contemporary images with various materials and forms, embodying unique stories crafted by the artists. Their creations capture the personal joy, wishes, and happiness evoked by moon jars while incorporating diverse perspectives through subjective creativity. The three artists are forging a new wave in tradition, harmoniously blending inherited values with contemporary narratives. Using moon jars as a medium, each artist conveys their unique artistic value and cultural expression, infusing unchanging values with new emotions to deliver their distinctive messages. Amid rapid changes, we invite you to fully experience the jars created by three artists at Superior Gallery, where they skillfully blend their unique realms into the living, breathing fabric of everyday life.

desc_l10n.ko: 슈페리어갤러리는 전통의 지속성을 유지하면서 동시대의 새로운 생활예술로 발전시켜 이어 나가고 있는 강민성, 김경희, 조성현 작가의 《내 손 위의 Super Moon : 달항아리》 展을 기획하였습니다. 전통적 기법과 이미지를 현대적으로 재해석하여 다양한 소재와 형태로 현대적 이미지에 조형성을 접목하여 자신만의 스토리를 담은 작품들을 선보입니다. 이들의 작품은 달항아리가 주는 개인적인 기쁨, 소망, 행복을 담는 동시에 주관적 창의력에 다양한 시각을 담아냅니다. 세 작가는 새로운 전통의 흐름을 만들어내고 있으며, 이를 통해 이어온 가치를 현대적인 이야기로 조화롭게 접목하고 있습니다. 달항아리를 매개로 각자의 예술적 가치와 문화적 표현을 전달하며, 변하지 않는 가치에 새로운 감성을 더해 그들만의 메시지를 전달하고 있습니다. 급격한 변화의 흐름 속에서 고유한 영역을 살아 숨 쉬는 일상으로 녹여내는 세 작가의 항아리를 슈페리어갤러리에서 온전히 느껴보시길 바랍니다.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Open-Air Museum_Pungnap Welcome to Open-Air Museum_Pungnap. Here is Pungnaptoseong, an earthen mound built by the people of the Hanseong Baekje period to defend their city along the windy Han River. Over time, a city has been built within the fortress, burying traces of past eras underground. With relics buried one to two meters below the surface, the inside of the fortress itself becomes a vast, hidden museum. Now, please take a moment to imagine this immense museum, and remember that a museum has exhibition halls where relics or artworks are displayed. This exhibition envisions the excavation sites within the fortress as exhibition halls. That said, these halls come to be sites where visitors encounter contemporary artworks while walking along the streets or turning a corner, thus blending the past with the present. So, what kind of works would you expect to encounter in such a museum? This exhibition consists of “reappearing” works that can metaphorically represent the characteristics of space and time. You will encounter the emergence of traditional media experiments, historical works, images, and others. In today’s time of immense interest in nonlinear temporality, the exhibition showcases works by artists who have meticulously experimented with and restructured the content, form, and structure of traditional media in the Korean art scene; these works metaphorically and materially represent the layers of time and space in contemporary Pungnap-dong. Additionally, it explores the spatial boundaries of art and museums by installing mediums such as Korean painting, painting, video, photography, and ceramics, which are usually exhibited indoors, outdoors. These works by the mound are realized like small openings to a portal to another time and space, with even the flow of the wind between them becoming visible. Artist Seung-taek Lee, who has established a unique artistic practice through the concept of “non-art,” presents another track in this exhibition by circulating through the city. Lee’s bicycle carrying the earth symbolizes the reappearance of historical works and becomes a ritual of circulation. To add, Lee’s wind extends beyond the city to the fortress; the red cloth flying across the wind, along with the earth running through the fortress, reaches back to a time older than the Hanseong Baekje period, older than ancient times, making one perceive the planet Earth and its life. How did you feel after walking through this vast museum and discovering the hidden artworks? We hope this exhibition provides an opportunity for you to transform your view of Pungnaptoseong, a historical yet everyday space, and discover new possibilities within the city. □ Performance information Open Air Museum_Pungnap is pleased to present renactments of Seung-taek Lee's iconic reproduced works, Wind-Folk Amusement (1971) and Earth Play (1994). These are visualizations of ""Wind,"" a red cloth that forms the shape of a bicycle and wind carrying an PVC balloon. It will be held four times on August 24, August 31, October 4, and October 11, and anyone can watch Earth, Let's Play from 15:00 to 16:00 and Wind, Let's Play from 16:00 to 16:30 at the Pungnaptoseong Namseong-Wall.

left: 0px} 《オープンエアミュージアム_プンナプトソン(風納土城)》にお越しいただき、ありがとうございます。 こちらはプンナプトソン(風納土城)です。プンナプトソン(風納土城)は、ハンソンベクチェ(漢城百済)時代に、風が吹くハンガン(漢江)沿いに都市を築いた人々が、都市の防御のために土で積み上げて作った丘です。今日に至るまで、土城の内部には都市が重ねられ、この時代の痕跡は地下に埋もれています。地表面から1～2メートル下には遺構が埋もれており、土城の内部はそれ自体が見えない巨大な博物館となっています。 この巨大な博物館を想像してみてください。博物館には、遺物や作品を展示する展示室があることも思い起こしてください。今回の展示は、土城内部の遺構発掘予定地を一つの展示室として想像します。この展示室は、観覧者が道を歩いたり、路地を回りながら、同時代の美術作品と出会う空間であり、過去から現在に至る時間が融合する場所です。 それでは、皆さんはどのような作品と出会うことを期待していますか？今回の展示は、空間と時間の特性を比喩することができる、「再出没」する作品で構成されています。皆さんは、さまざまな場所で伝統的メディアの実験の出没、歴史的作品の出没、イメージの出没、他者の出没と遭遇することになるでしょう。非線形的な時間性に対する関心が高まる現代において、これらの作品は韓国美術界で長年にわたり伝統的メディアの内容、形式、構造を繊細に実験し再構築してきた作家たちの作品であり、同時代のプンナプドン(風納洞)の時間と地層を比喩し、具現化しています。また、通常は室内で展示される韓国画、絵画、映像、写真、陶芸などのジャンルを屋外に新たに具現しながら、アートと美術館の空間的な境界を探求します。 異なる時空間へのポータルが開かれるように出没する作品とともに、これらの作品の間を吹く風の流れも可視化されます。「非美術」という概念で独自の作品世界を築いてきたイ・スンテク作家の作品は、今回の展示のもう一つのトラックとして都市を循環します。地球を載せて走る自転車は、歴史的作品の再出没であり、循環の意識となります。また、イ・スンテク作家の風は、都市内部だけでなく土城にまで広がります。土城を走る地球と風に乗って飛ぶ赤い布は、ハンソンベクチェ(漢城百済)時代よりもさらに古い、古代よりもさらに古い時代に到達し、地球という惑星とその生命を感じさせます。 隠れた作品を発見しながら、これまでの巨大なミュージアムを一緒に歩いてきた感想はいかがでしたか？今回の展示が、プンナプトソン(風納土城)という歴史的かつ日常的な空間のシーンを変換し、都市の新しい可能性を発見する機会となることを願っています。 □ パフォーマンスのご案内 今回の展示では、「非美術」という概念で独自の作品世界を築いてきた韓国美術界の巨匠、イ・スンテク作家の歴史的屋外パフォーマンス作品である<風よ、遊ぼう>、<地球よ、遊ぼう>をプンナプドン(風納洞)とプンナプトソン(風納土城)で新たに再演します。これらの作品は「風」を可視化した作品で、アドバルーンの地球を載せて走る自転車と風の形を具現化する赤い布です。 8月24日、8月31日、10月4日、10月11日の4回実施され、<地球よ、遊ぼう>は15:00-16:00、<風よ、遊ぼう>は16:00-16:30までプンナプトソン(風納土城)の南城壁で誰でも観覧できます。 ※ パフォーマンスの映像は、ソウル市立美術館のYouTubeチャンネルで9月初旬に公開予定です。 - 振付: キム・ヘヨン - 振付助手および出演: オ・ジョンユン - 出演: チェ・テホン、キム・ミンジョン、コ・ウンス、オ・チャンヤン、パク・スビン、キム・ヨンヨン、ジ・セヨン
desc_l10n.ko: 《오픈 에어 뮤지엄_풍납토성》에 방문하신 여러분을 환영합니다. 이곳은 풍납토성입니다. 풍납토성은 한성백제 시대, 바람 부는 한강변에 도시를 지은 사람들이 도시의 방어를 위해 흙으로 쌓아 만든 언덕입니다. 오늘에 이르기까지 토성의 안쪽으로는 도시가 덧세워지며 이 시대의 흔적은 지하에 묻히게 되었습니다. 지표면에서 1–2m 아래 유구들이 묻혀있기에, 토성 안은 그 자체로 드러나지 않은 거대한 박물관이 됩니다. 이제 거대한 박물관을 상상해주시기 바랍니다. 박물관에는 유물이나 작품을 전시하는 전시실이 있다는 점도 떠올려주시기 바랍니다. 이번 전시는 토성 내부의 유구 발굴 예정지를 하나의 전시실로 상상합니다. 이 전시실은 관람객이 길을 걷다가 또는 골목을 돌다가 동시대 미술 작품의 출현과 맞닥뜨리게 되는 공간이자 그로 인해 과거로부터 현재에 이르는 시간이 융합되는 장소입니다. 그렇다면 여러분은 어떤 작품과 맞닥뜨리는 것을 기대하시나요? 이번 전시는 공간과 시간의 특성을 은유할 수 있는, ‘재출몰’하는 작품들로 구성되었습니다. 여러분은 여러 장소에서 전통 매체 실험의 출몰, 역사적 작품의 출몰, 이미지의 출몰, 타자의 출몰과 조우하게 됩니다. 비선형적인 시간성에 대한 관심이 큰 요즘, 이 작품들은 이전부터 한국 미술계에서 섬세하게 전통적 매체의 내용, 형식, 구조를 실험하고 재구성해 온 작가들의 작품이며, 동시대 풍납동의 시간과 지층을 은유하고 물질화합니다. 또한 보통 실내에서 전시되는 한국화, 회화, 영상, 사진, 도자 등의 장르를 야외에 새롭게 구현하면서 미술과 미술관의 공간적 경계를 탐험합니다. 다른 시공간으로의 포털이 열리듯 출몰하는 작품들과 더불어 이들 사이를 부는 바람의 흐름 역시 가시화됩니다. ‘비미술’이라는 개념으로 독자적 작품 세계를 구축해 온 이승택 작가의 작품은 이번 전시의 또 하나의 트랙으로서 도시를 순환합니다. 지구를 싣고 달리는 자전거는 역사적 작품의 재출몰이면서 순환의 의식이 됩니다. 또한 이승택 작가의 바람은 도시 내부뿐 아니라 토성에까지 폭을 넓힙니다. 토성을 달리는 지구와 바람을 타고 나는 붉은 천은 한성 백제 시대보다 더 오랜, 고대보다 더 오랜 시기에 가 닿아 지구라는 행성과 그 생명을 감각하게 합니다. 숨어있는 작품들을 발견하며 지금까지 거대한 뮤지엄을 함께 걸으신 느낌은 어떠셨나요? 이번 전시가 여러분께 풍납토성이라는 역사적이면서 일상적인 공간의 장면을 전환하고 도시의 새로운 가능성을 발견할 수 있는 기회가 되기를 바랍니다. □ 퍼포먼스 안내 이번 전시에는 ‘비미술’이라는 개념으로 독자적 작품 세계를 구축해온 한국미술계의 거장 이승택 작가의 역사적 야외 퍼포먼스 작품인 <바람아 놀자>, <지구야 놀자>를 풍납동과 풍납토성에서 새롭게 재연합니다. 이 작품들은 ‘바람’을 가시화한 작품들로 애드벌룬 지구를 싣고 달리는 자전거와 바람의 형태를 조형화하는 붉은 천입니다. 8월 24일, 8월 31일, 10월 4일, 10월 11일 총 4회 진행되며 <지구야 놀자>는 15:00~16:00, <바람아 놀자>는 16:00-16:30까지 풍납토성 남성벽에서 누구나 관람하실 수 있습니다. ※ 퍼포먼스 영상은 서울시립미술관 유튜브 채널을 통해 9월 초에 공개될 예정입니다. - 안무: 김혜연- 조안무 및 출연: 오정윤- 출연: 최태헌, 김민정, 고은수, 오찬양, 박수빈, 김연영, 지세영
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 欢迎来到《开放空间博物馆 风纳土城》。 这里是风纳土城。风纳土城是汉城百济时代，为了防御城市而在风吹的汉江边用土堆砌而成的丘陵。随着时间的推移，土城内侧逐渐被建成城市，那个时代的痕迹被埋藏在地下。在地表下1-2米的地方埋藏着遗迹，因此这片土城本身就是一个未揭示的巨大博物馆。 现在请想象这个巨大的博物馆。请记住，博物馆中有展示文物或艺术品的展厅。此次展览将土城内部的遗迹发掘预定地想象为一个展厅。这个展厅是让观众在漫步或转角时，与同时代的艺术作品不期而遇的空间，同时也是过去与现在时间交融的地方。 那么，您期待会遇到什么样的作品呢？此次展览由能够隐喻空间和时间特性的‘再次出现’的作品组成。您将在多个地点邂逅传统媒介实验的出现、历史作品的出现、图像的出现、他者的出现。在当今对非线性时间性的关注日益增大的情况下，这些作品是韩国艺术界从前就细腻地实验并重构传统媒介内容、形式和结构的艺术家们的作品，同时隐喻并物化了当代风纳洞的时间和地层。此外，这些通常在室内展出的韩国画、绘画、影像、摄影、陶瓷等类型的作品被全新地呈现在户外，探索了艺术与美术馆的空间界限。 随着这些如同打开通往其他时空的门户般出现的作品，流动在它们之间的风的轨迹也被视觉化了。通过‘非美术’这一概念构筑了独立艺术世界的艺术家Lee Seung taek的作品，是此次展览的另一条轨迹。载着地球的自行车既是历史作品的再现，也是循环的仪式。而Lee Seung taek的风不仅扩展到了城市内部，还延伸到了土城。骑行在土城的地球与随风飘扬的红布，使人感受到比汉城百济时代更久远、比古代更悠久的时期，感知地球这个星球及其生命。 在发现隐藏的作品，并与我们一同漫步于这个巨大的博物馆之后，您感觉如何呢？希望此次展览能为您带来转换风纳土城这一历史且日常空间的场景，并发现城市新可能的机会。 □ 表演指南 此次展览将重新演绎在韩国艺术界通过‘非美术’这一概念构筑了独特艺术世界的大师Lee Seung taek的历史性户外表演作品《风儿玩吧》和《地球啊玩吧》，地点在风纳洞与风纳土城。这些作品是将‘风’视觉化的作品，展示了载着广告气球地球的自行车和塑造风的形态的红布。 表演将在8月24日、8月31日、10月4日、10月11日共4次进行，《地球啊玩吧》将于15:00-16:00，《风儿玩吧》将于16:00-16:30在风纳土城南城墙上向公众开放，所有人都可以观赏。 ※ 表演视频将在9月初通过首尔市立美术馆YouTube频道公开。 - 编舞：Kim Hye yeon - 协助编舞及出演：Oh Jung yun - 出演：Choi Tae heon, Kim Min jung, Go Eun soo, Oh Chan yang, Park Soo bin, Kim Yeon young, Ji Se young

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Open-Air Museum_Pungnap Welcome to Open-Air Museum_Pungnap. Here is Pungnaptoseong, an earthen mound built by the people of the Hanseong Baekje period to defend their city along the windy Han River. Over time, a city has been built within the fortress, burying traces of past eras underground. With relics buried one to two meters below the surface, the inside of the fortress itself becomes a vast, hidden museum. Now, please take a moment to imagine this immense museum, and remember that a museum has exhibition halls where relics or artworks are displayed. This exhibition envisions the excavation sites within the fortress as exhibition halls. That said, these halls come to be sites where visitors encounter contemporary artworks while walking along the streets or turning a corner, thus blending the past with the present. So, what kind of works would you expect to encounter in such a museum? This exhibition consists of “reappearing” works that can metaphorically represent the characteristics of space and time. You will encounter the emergence of traditional media experiments, historical works, images, and others. In today’s time of immense interest in nonlinear temporality, the exhibition showcases works by artists who have meticulously experimented with and restructured the content, form, and structure of traditional media in the Korean art scene; these works metaphorically and materially represent the layers of time and space in contemporary Pungnap-dong. Additionally, it explores the spatial boundaries of art and museums by installing mediums such as Korean painting, painting, video, photography, and ceramics, which are usually exhibited indoors, outdoors. These works by the mound are realized like small openings to a portal to another time and space, with even the flow of the wind between them becoming visible. Artist Seung-taek Lee, who has established a unique artistic practice through the concept of “non-art,” presents another track in this exhibition by circulating through the city. Lee’s bicycle carrying the earth symbolizes the reappearance of historical works and becomes a ritual of circulation. To add, Lee’s wind extends beyond the city to the fortress; the red cloth flying across the wind, along with the earth running through the fortress, reaches back to a time older than the Hanseong Baekje period, older than ancient times, making one perceive the planet Earth and its life. How did you feel after walking through this vast museum and discovering the hidden artworks? We hope this exhibition provides an opportunity for you to transform your view of Pungnaptoseong, a historical yet everyday space, and discover new possibilities within the city. □ Performance information Open Air Museum_Pungnap is pleased to present renactments of Seung-taek Lee's iconic reproduced works, Wind-Folk Amusement (1971) and Earth Play (1994). These are visualizations of ""Wind,"" a red cloth that forms the shape of a bicycle and wind carrying an PVC balloon. It will be held four times on August 24, August 31, October 4, and October 11, and anyone can watch Earth, Let's Play from 15:00 to 16:00 and Wind, Let's Play from 16:00 to 16:30 at the Pungnaptoseong Namseong-Wall.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} The 20th-anniversary exhibition of the Seoul Museum of Art's Nanji Residency, 《The Origin of Love (AMOR EX MACHINA)》, is structured as a journey to look back on the meaning of love by borrowing the archetypes of old stories in an era where technology rewrites relationships. Technology is no longer a tool placed outside of life, but has become an environment that conditions our senses and relationships. We wake up to smartphone alarms, move along paths indicated by satellites, and spend our days encountering news selected by algorithms. Within this, the ways we remember and form relationships are also changing. The exhibition proposes that our destination amidst the changing landscape of technology lies in love, the sense that makes us human.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} ソウル市立美術館ナンジ(蘭芝)美術創作スタジオ開館20周年記念展《愛の起源 AMOR EX MACHINA》は、技術が関係を書き換える時代、古い物語の原型を借りて愛の意味を振り返る旅路として構成されています。技術は人生の外側に置かれた道具ではなく、感覚と関係を条件づける環境となりました。私たちはスマートフォンのアラームで目覚め、衛星が示す道に従って動き、アルゴリズムが選んだニュースに接して一日を過ごします。その中で、私たちが記憶し関係を結ぶ方法も共に変化していきます。本展は、変化する技術の風景の中で、私たちの目的地が私たちを人間たらしめる感覚、すなわち愛にあることを提案します。
desc_l10n.ko: 서울시립미술관 난지미술창작스튜디오 개관 20주년 기념전 《사랑의 기원 AMOR EX MACHINA》은 기술이 관계를 고쳐 쓰는 시대, 오래된 이야기의 원형을 빌려 사랑의 의미를 다시 돌아보는 여정으로 구성됩니다. 기술은 삶의 바깥에 놓인 도구가 아니라 감각과 관계를 조건 짓는 환경이 되었습니다. 스마트폰 알람으로 잠에서 깨고, 위성이 가리키는 길을 따라 움직이며, 알고리즘이 골라낸 소식을 접하며 하루를 보냅니다. 그 안에서 우리가 기억하고 관계 맺는 방식도 함께 바뀌어 갑니다. 전시는 변화하는 기술의 풍경 속에서 우리의 목적지가 우리를 인간이게 하는 감각, 사랑에 있음을 제안합니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 首尔市立美术馆兰芝美术创作工作室开馆20周年纪念展《爱的起源：AMOR EX MACHINA》，立足于科技重塑人际联结的时代背景，借经典古老故事的原型，开启一场重新审视爱之内涵的艺术之旅。科技早已不再是游离于生活之外的工具，转而成为左右人类感知和关系的环境。我们伴着手机闹钟苏醒，循着卫星导航前行，整日浏览算法筛选推送的资讯。身处这样的环境，人类的记忆模式与人际交往方式也随之悄然改变。本展意在点明，在日新月异的科技图景之中，能够成就人之本性的感官、名为爱的羁绊，才是我们最终的归宿。

Technology is no longer a tool placed outside of life, but has become an environment that conditions our senses and relationships. We wake up to smartphone alarms, move along paths indicated by satellites, and spend our days encountering news selected by algorithms. Within this, the ways we remember and form relationships are also changing. The exhibition proposes that our destination amidst the changing landscape of technology lies in love, the sense that makes us human.

This exhibition is held under the theme of IN-BETWEEN in collaboration with three artists; Nikki S. Lee, Christine Sun Kim, and Emmanuel Hahn. IN-BETWEEN carries a layered meaning, combining “IN” (inside) and “BE” (to exist), and delves into questions of identity, boundaries, and human consciousness. The three contemporary artists, each gaining attention in the art world, reexamine the space of “boundaries” from their own perspectives. Experience their exploration through photography, video, and drawing in BAZAAR Exhibition, IN-BETWEEN.

desc_l10n.ko: 패션 매거진 <하퍼스 바자>의 세 번째 전시회. 이번 전시는 <IN-BETWEEN>을 주제로 3인의 작가들(니키 리, 크리스틴 선 킴, 엠마누엘 한)과 함께 합니다. 'IN-BETWEEN(인-비트윈)'은 '사이(IN)'와 '존재하다(BE)'를 결합한 중의적 의미를 통해 정체성과 경계, 그리고 인간의 존재 의식에 대한 이야기를 담고 있습니다. 현대 미술에서 주목받는 세 명의 작가가 각자의 시선으로 ‘경계’의 공간을 다시 들여다봅니다. 사진, 영상, 드로잉 등 각기 다른 시선으로 탐색한 작품들을 <바자전: IN-BETWEEN>에서 만나보세요.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} At the End of the World Splits Endlessly seeks to interpret SeMA’s collection through the keywords of connection and combination between mediums. In this post-medium/post-media era, the exhibition explores the inevitable structure between artists and their works, mediated by technology, while showcasing the multi-layered structure of media today. It examines how old and new media, virtual and real, AI and the body, and the interplay of technology and society create complex media environments. The term "medium" originates from the Greek word for "middle" or "between," signifying how, in contemporary art, mediums function as a bridge—linking the artist, the artwork, the viewer, and the museum. As visitors follow the exhibition's key concepts—Old & New, Yellow Block, Layered Medium, Open End—it reveals our current media landscape's singular and plural structures. Inspired by anthropologist Anna Tsing’s The Mushroom at the End of the World and Jorge Luis Borges’ The Garden of Forking Paths, this exhibition grapples with the questions posed by the climate crisis and the end of capitalism. Through their works, artists ask where we stand in the world as it fractures. Just as artists traverse a spectrum of media, choosing and renewing their mediums, we, too, dream of new connections in a world that endlessly diverges. These connections, however, are not seamless but fragmented and partial. Art encourages us to confront this imperfection, urging us to find life, reflection, resistance, hope, and imagination among the ruins and potentialities of our time.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《果てしなく分岐する世界の終わりで》は、SeMAの所蔵品を「メディア間の連結と結合」というキーワードで読み解こうとする展覧会です。ポストミディウム/ポストメディア時代において、メディアを媒介としてアーティストと作品の必然的な構造を探求し、オールドメディアとニューメディア、仮想と現実、AIと身体など、技術と社会の変化に応じたメディアが生み出す我々の時代の媒体/メディアの多層的な構造を示します。メディアの語源は、ギリシャ語で中間を意味する「medium」や、間にあることを意味する「medius」から来ています。現代アートにおいて媒体は、媒介、媒材、霊媒、連結として、作品とアーティスト、作品と観覧客、観覧客と美術館を結ぶ複雑な結合の層を成します。「オールド&ニュー」「イエローブロック」「レイヤードミディウム」「オープンエンド」といった展覧会のキーワードをたどっていくと、今/ここにおける媒体的状況は単数かつ複数の重層的構造として存在していることがわかります。 人類学者アナ・チンの『世界の終わりのキノコ』とホルヘ・ルイス・ボルヘスの小説『分岐する小径の庭』にインスパイアされたこの展覧会のタイトルのように、気候危機と資本主義の終焉、世界の果てでアーティストたちは私たちがどこに立っているのかを芸術を通じて問いかけています。メディアを選択して更新する過程で、アーティストたちがさまざまな振幅を超えながら作品を作り上げていくように、果てしなく分かれゆく世界の中で私たちは逆説的に新たな連結を夢見るのです。それは完璧に繋がった隙間のないつながりではなく、すでに部分的で壊れた連結です。芸術はまさにその不完全さや不十分さを再び見つめ直させ、その残骸の廃墟の中で依然としてうごめく生命、反省、抵抗、希望、想像といった潜在的可能性について私たちに語りかけています。
desc_l10n.ko: 《끝없이 갈라지는 세계의 끝에서》는 SeMA 소장품을 매체 사이의 연결과 결합이라는 키워드로 읽어내고자 합니다. 포스트-미디엄/포스트-미디어 시대 매체를 매개로 예술가와 작품의 필연적 구조를 탐색하고, 올드미디어와 뉴미디어, 가상과 현실, AI와 신체 등 기술과 사회의 변화에 조응하는 매체가 만들어내는 우리 시대 매체/미디어의 다층적 구조를 보여주는 전시입니다. 매체의 어원은 그리스어로 가운데라는 의미의 메디움(medium), 사이에 있다는 뜻의 메디우스(medius)에서 유래했습니다. 현대미술에서 매체는 매개, 매질, 영매, 연결로서 작품과 작가, 작품과 관람자, 관람자와 미술관을 이어내는 복합적인 연결의 층들을 구성합니다. 올드 앤 뉴, 옐로우 블록, 레이어드 미디엄, 오픈 앤드와 같은 전시의 키워드들을 클릭하듯 따라가면 지금/여기의 매체적 상황은 단수이자 복수인 중층적 구조로 존재한다는 것을 살펴볼 수 있습니다. 인류학자 애나 칭의 『세계 끝의 버섯』과 호르헤 보르헤스의 소설 『끝없이 두 갈래로 갈라지는 길들이 있는 정원』에서 영감을 받은 전시의 제목처럼 기후 위기와 자본주의의 막바지, 세계의 끝에서 예술가들은 우리가 어디에 서 있는지 예술을 통해 묻고 있습니다. 매체를 선택하고 갱신하는 과정에서 예술가들이 다양한 진폭을 넘나드는 고민 끝에서 작품을 만들어가듯이 끝없이 갈라지는 세계 속에서 우리는 역설적으로 새로운 연결을 꿈꾸게 됩니다. 그것은 완벽히 이어진 빈틈없는 연결이 아닌 이미 부분적이고 부서진 연결입니다. 예술은 바로 그 불완전하고 불충분함을 다시금 바라보라고, 그 잔해의 폐허 속에서 여전히 꿈틀대는 어떤 생명, 성찰, 저항, 희망, 상상 그 어떤 잠재적 가능성에 대하여 우리에게 말을 건네고 있습니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 《无限分裂的世界尽头》将SEMA收藏品以媒体之间的连接和结合为关键词进行解读。以后媒体/后媒体时代媒体为媒介，探索艺术家和作品的必然结构，展示老媒体和新媒体、虚拟和现实、AI和身体等适应技术和社会变化的媒体创造的我们时代媒体/媒体的多层结构的展览。媒体的词源来源于希腊语中意为中间的medium和介于中间的medius。在现代美术中，媒体作为媒介、媒介、灵媒、连接，构成连接作品和作家、作品和观众、观众和美术馆的综合连接的层。像点击老&新、黄块、层叠式中号、开放式等展示关键词一样,可以看到现在/这里的媒体状况是以单数和复数的中层结构存在的。正如从人类学家安清的《在世界尽头遇到松茸》和豪尔赫·博尔赫斯的小说《小径分岔的花园》中获得灵感的展览题目一样，气候危机和资本主义的最后阶段,艺术家们正在通过艺术询问我们站在哪里。在选择和更新媒体的过程中，就像艺术家们在经过多种幅度的苦恼后创作作品一样，在无休止的分裂世界中，我们反过来梦想着新的连接。那不是完美连接的严密连接，而是已经部分破碎的连接。艺术就是让我们重新审视其不完整和不充分，对于残骸废墟中依然蠕动的某种生命、反省、抵抗、希望、想象以及某种潜在的可能性，都在告诉我们。

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} At the End of the World Splits Endlessly seeks to interpret SeMA’s collection through the keywords of connection and combination between mediums. In this post-medium/post-media era, the exhibition explores the inevitable structure between artists and their works, mediated by technology, while showcasing the multi-layered structure of media today. It examines how old and new media, virtual and real, AI and the body, and the interplay of technology and society create complex media environments. The term "medium" originates from the Greek word for "middle" or "between," signifying how, in contemporary art, mediums function as a bridge—linking the artist, the artwork, the viewer, and the museum. As visitors follow the exhibition's key concepts—Old & New, Yellow Block, Layered Medium, Open End—it reveals our current media landscape's singular and plural structures. Inspired by anthropologist Anna Tsing’s The Mushroom at the End of the World and Jorge Luis Borges’ The Garden of Forking Paths, this exhibition grapples with the questions posed by the climate crisis and the end of capitalism. Through their works, artists ask where we stand in the world as it fractures. Just as artists traverse a spectrum of media, choosing and renewing their mediums, we, too, dream of new connections in a world that endlessly diverges. These connections, however, are not seamless but fragmented and partial. Art encourages us to confront this imperfection, urging us to find life, reflection, resistance, hope, and imagination among the ruins and potentialities of our time.

It includes works such as “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)”, “Anne of Green Gables (1979)”, “Grave of the Fireflies (1988)”, “Only Yesterday (1991)”, “Pom Poko (1994)”, and “The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013)”. His directorial materials include layouts, which can be likened to blueprints for animated film production, and sketches and handwritten notes that he wrote and drew. In addition, it is packed with previously unreleased materials from Miyazaki Hayao, who was responsible for the layouts during Takahata Isao's directorial era at Zuiyo Video, including “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)” and “Anne of Green Gables (1979).”

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} This exhibition showcases the entire production process of all the works directed by the master of animation, Takahata Isao, from his debut to his masterpieces. It includes works such as “Heidi, Girl of the Alps (1974)”, “Anne of Green Gables (1979)”, “Grave of the Fireflies (1988)”, “Only Yesterday (1991)”, “Pom Poko (1994)”, and “The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013)”. desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, is a historic performance hall in Jung-gu, Seoul. Originally opened in 1976 as Cecil Theater, it’s a small yet iconic venue with a capacity of 232 seats. During the late 1970s, it became the heart of Korea's theater scene, hosting the Korea Theater Festival from 1977 to 1980. Despite its prominence, financial difficulties led to its closure in 2018 after being operated by private theater groups 'Madan' and 'Rodem.' In April 2018, the Seoul Metropolitan Government spearheaded a cultural regeneration project to reopen Cecil Theater and handed its management to a non-profit organization. Designed by renowned architect Kim Joong-up, the theater has long been a cornerstone of Korean performing arts and cultural heritage. In 2022, the theater was revitalized under the management of the National Jeongdong Theater, taking on the new name 'National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil.' Today, it serves as a vibrant space for artists and audiences to connect through innovative and experimental performances, upholding its legacy and creative core values.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} セシル劇場は1976年に開館したソウル市チュン(中)区の演劇専用劇場で、座席数232席の小劇場です。1977年から1980年まで大韓民国演劇祭を開催し、1970年代の演劇界の中心となりました。その後、民間劇団の「マダン」と「ロデム」が運営を担当していましたが、財政難により2018年に閉館しました。しかし、ソウル市は2018年4月に「文化再生」を通じてセシル劇場を再開館し、非営利団体に運営を委託しました。この劇場は建築家キム・ジュンオプ氏により作られ、韓国の演劇や文化遺産において重要な役割を果たしてきました。その後、旧セシル劇場は2022年に国立チョンドン(貞洞)劇場が運営を引き継ぎ、「国立チョンドン劇場セシル」として生まれ変わりました。そして芸術家と観客を一つの作品として繋げる創作の価値として、様々な舞台が行われる場所となりました。
desc_l10n.ko: 세실극장은 1976년에 개관한 서울 중구의 연극 전용 공연장으로, 232석 규모의 소극장입니다. 1977년부터 1980년까지 대한민국연극제를 개최하며 1970년대 연극계의 중심이 되었고 이후 민간극단 '민간극단 '마당'과 '로뎀'이 운영을 맡았으나, 재정난으로 2018년 폐관되었습니다. 그러나 서울시는 2018년 4월 '문화재생'을 통해 세실극장을 재개관하고, 비영리 단체에 운영을 맡겼습니다. 이 극장은 건축가 김중업의 작품으로, 한국 연극과 문화유산에 중요한 역할을 해온 공간입니다. 이후 구)세실극장에서 2022년 국립정동극장이 운영을 맡아 '국립정동극장 세실'로 재탄생되었으며 예술가와 관객을 하나의 작품으로 이어주는 창작 핵심가치로써 다양한 창작자들의 도전적이고 실험적인 무대가 펼쳐지는 공간입니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Cecil剧场是位于首尔中区的话剧专用剧场，于1976年开馆，拥有232个座位。自1977年至1980年间，该剧场成功举办了大韩民国戏剧节，并在1970年代成为了戏剧界的中心。此后，它由民间剧团“Madang”和“Rodem”负责运营，但遗憾的是，由于财政困难，Cecil剧场于2018年被迫闭馆。然而，在2018年4月，首尔市通过“文化再生”项目重新开馆了Cecil剧场，并将其运营委托给了一个非营利团体。这座剧场是建筑师金重业的杰作，一直以来都对韩国话剧和文化遗产的发展起到了重要作用。到了2022年，Cecil剧场的运营权转交给了国立贞洞剧场，并重新命名为“国立贞洞剧场Cecil”。它现在不仅是连接艺术家与观众的桥梁，更是展现创作者挑战性、实验性舞台作品的核心价值所在，为多种艺术形式的探索和表达提供了宝贵的空间。

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > *, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Newly established in Gwanghwamun Square, the Garden of Gratitude is a space designed to reflect upon the gratitude toward Korean War veterans and the achievements and prosperity of the Republic of Korea, which has transitioned from an aid-recipient country to a donor country. The "Light of Gratitude 23" comprises 23 symbolic sculptures situated quietly yet magnificently at the center of Gwanghwamun Square. It stands as a symbol of the deepest respect and gratitude dedicated to the noble devotion of the participating nations that willingly extended their hands to safeguard the freedom and peace of the Republic of Korea. "Freedom Hall," situated underground at Gwanghwamun Square, is an immersive multimedia space where visitors can multi-dimensionally experience the sentiments of freedom, sacrifice, peace, and gratitude toward the nations that participated in the Korean War.
desc_l10n.ko: 광화문광장에 새롭게 조성된 감사의 정원은 6 ·25 전쟁 참전용사에 대한 감사와, 도움 받던 나라에서 도움을 드리는 나라로 도약한 대한민국의 성과와 번영을 되새기는 공간입니다. 감사의 빛 23은 광화문광장의 중심에 고요하면서도 웅장하게 자리 잡은 23개의 상징조형물으로, 대한민국의 자유와 평화를 수호하기 위해 기꺼이 손을 내밀었던 참전국들의 숭고한 헌신에 바치는 가장 깊은 경의이자 감사의 표상입니다. 광화문광장 지하에 마련된 프리덤 홀은 한국전쟁 참전국에 대한 자유, 희생, 평화, 감사의 마음을 입체적으로 체험할 수 있는 복합 미디어 공간입니다.

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} This landmark exhibition celebrates 60 years of normalized diplomatic relations between Korea and Japan and the 80th anniversary of Korea’s liberation. It serves as a meaningful moment to reflect on the Korea-Japan relationship. While Japan remains Korea’s closest neighbor, many unresolved issues still hinder deeper cooperation. The more we reflect on the past and examine the present, the better we can prepare for a new turning point. 'Bonds of the Heart, Waves of Resonance' explores the essence of trust and exchange—between nations and between individuals—through the story of the Tongsinsa, the diplomatic missions of the Joseon Dynasty. While Tongsinsa refers to formal diplomatic delegations and systems, their deeper significance goes beyond diplomacy and cultural exchange. These missions were based on mutual respect, trust, and understanding, fostering friendship between nations and bonds between people. History is not merely a record of the past—it is a force that connects the present and future. Through this historical legacy of Tongsinsa, which bridges state and individual, diplomacy and culture, past and present, this exhibition reflects on the meaning of "diplomacy based on trust" and encourages us to envision a peaceful future together.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 日韓両国の平和外交、文化交流遺産として平和外交の余韻を再び残し、1985年以降40年ぶりの最大規模、朝鮮王朝時代の通信使遺産の集大成、ユネスコの「世界の記憶」など128点、国内外18機関の所蔵品が一堂に！ 世界的なアーティストの没入型映像と家族みんなで楽しむ体験コンテンツまで体験できます。 今年は日韓国交正常化60周年、終戦80周年を迎える年で、日本との関係を振り返るのに意味深い時期です。日本は最も近い隣国ですが、両国の関係をさらに一歩進めるためには解決しなければならない課題が依然として多いです。過去を振り返り、現在を省察する過程が積み重なるほど、新たな転換点を迎えることができるでしょう。 「心のつきあい、余韻が波のように」は朝鮮王朝時代の通信使を通じて国家間、そして個人間の信頼と交流の意味にスポットを当てています。通信使は朝鮮王朝時代の外交使節団であり、外交システムを意味しますが、その本質は単なる外交と文化交流を超えています。信頼と尊重、相互理解を基に持続的な関係を結ぶことで、国家間の友好を形成し、個人間の絆をさらに深めてきたからです。 歴史は単なる過去の記録ではなく、現在と未来をつなぐ力です。国から個人へ、外交から文化交流へ、過去から現在へと続く通信使の歴史的遺産を通じて、信頼を基盤に平和を模索した「通信使外交」の意味を振り返り、今後の道を共に考える機会になることを期待します。
desc_l10n.ko: 한일 양국의 평화외교, 문화교류 유산으로 평화외교의 여운을 다시 이어 1985년 이후 40년 만의 최대 규모, 조선시대 통신사 유산 집대성, 유네스코 세계기록유산 등 128점, 국내외 18개 기관 소장품 한자리에! 세계적 아티스트의 몰입형 영상과 온 가족이 즐기는 체험 콘텐츠까지 경험 할 수 있습니다. 올해는 한일 국교 정상화 60주년, 광복 80주년을 맞이하는 해로, 일본과의 관계를 되돌아보기에 뜻깊은 시점입니다. 일본은 가장 가까운 이웃이지만, 양국 관계를 한 걸음 더 진전시키기 위해서는 여전히 해결해야 할 과제가 많습니다. 과거를 돌아보고 현재를 성찰하는 과정이 쌓일수록, 새로운 전환점을 마련할 수 있을 것입니다. '마음의 사귐, 여운이 물결처럼'은 조선시대 통신사(通信使)를 통해 국가 간, 그리고 개인 간 신뢰와 교류의 의미를 조명합니다. 통신사는 조선시대 외교 사절단이자 외교 시스템을 의미하지만, 그 본질은 단순한 외교와 문화교류를 넘어섭니다. 신뢰와 존중, 상호 이해를 바탕으로 지속적인 관계를 맺음으로써 국가 간 우호를 형성하고, 개인 간 유대를 더욱 단단히 이어왔기 때문입니다. 역사는 단순한 과거의 기록이 아니라, 현재와 미래를 연결하는 힘입니다. 국가에서 개인으로, 외교에서 문화교류로, 과거에서 현재로 이어지는 통신사의 역사적 유산을 통해, 신뢰를 기반으로 평화를 모색했던 '통신사 외교'의 의미를 되새기며, 앞으로의 길을 함께 고민하는 기회가 되기를 기대합 니다.
desc_l10n.zh: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 通过韩日两国和平外交，文化交流遗产，再次传承和平外交的余韵，自1985年后40年来最大规模的展览，朝鲜时代通信使遗产集大成，128件联合国教科文组织世界记忆遗产、国内外18件机构收藏品齐聚一堂！ 访客还可以体验世界艺术家的沉浸式视频，以及全家尽情享受的体验内容。 今年是韩日邦交正常化60周年，光复80周年，在回顾与日本的关系时具有深远意义。虽然日本是最近的邻国，但为了进一步推进两国关系，仍然有很多问题需要解决。越是回顾过去、反思现在的过程，越有可能出现新的转机。 “心灵之交，余韵似涟漪”通过朝鲜时代通信使，展现国家之间和个人间的信赖和交流意义。通信使是朝鲜时代的外交使团和外交系统，但其本质已经超越了单纯的外交和文化交流。在信任和尊重、相互理解的基础上建立持久关系，形成国家之间的友好关系，更加牢固地建立了个人间的纽带。 历史不仅仅是对过去的记录，更是连接现在和未来的力量。期待通过从国家到个人、从外交到文化交流、从过去到现在的通信使的历史遗产，重温以信任为基础探索和平的“通信使外交”的意义，成为共同思考未来道路的机会。

description: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} This landmark exhibition celebrates 60 years of normalized diplomatic relations between Korea and Japan and the 80th anniversary of Korea’s liberation. It serves as a meaningful moment to reflect on the Korea-Japan relationship. While Japan remains Korea’s closest neighbor, many unresolved issues still hinder deeper cooperation. The more we reflect on the past and examine the present, the better we can prepare for a new turning point. 'Bonds of the Heart, Waves of Resonance' explores the essence of trust and exchange—between nations and between individuals—through the story of the Tongsinsa, the diplomatic missions of the Joseon Dynasty. While Tongsinsa refers to formal diplomatic delegations and systems, their deeper significance goes beyond diplomacy and cultural exchange. These missions were based on mutual respect, trust, and understanding, fostering friendship between nations and bonds between people. History is not merely a record of the past—it is a force that connects the present and future. Through this historical legacy of Tongsinsa, which bridges state and individual, diplomacy and culture, past and present, this exhibition reflects on the meaning of "diplomacy based on trust" and encourages us to envision a peaceful future together.
name: Bonds of the Heart, Waves of Resonance

desc_l10n.en: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} Stars are not abstract symbols in the distant sky, they are the very spot where I stand, breathing and living in the present moment. The small tremors and deep immersion we experience in everyday life create a resonance of consciousness, within which a universe, a world, emerges. This exhibition is a condensation of moments deepened and contemplated in prolonged silence and stillness. Time spent alone, detached from relationships, reflects the paths I have walked and the traces of pauses I have taken, while simultaneously serving as a gateway to another world. Within the context of traditional calligraphy, I evoke the primal forms and energies of ancient scripts, especially oracle bone characters, and reconstruct them with Hangul’s formal possibilities through a contemporary sensibility. The characters go beyond mere tools for communication; they manifest as traces of existence and as visual sculptural forms. Letters that breathe like living hearts engrave a pulse into each stroke, leaving trajectories that pierce through time. “Here, Standing on a Star” does not refer to any particular star. It is the “here” where I stand, the moments of now. The characters that bloom in this space transcend personal records and explore how humans perceive and sense the world. I hope this exhibition becomes, for visitors, another star and a pathway to their inner selves. Along this journey, I envision embracing even severed relationships without fear, and standing as a radiant being in one’s own right.
desc_l10n.ko: 별은 머나먼 하늘 위의 관념적 기호가 아니라, 지금 내가 서 있는 자리, 호흡하며 살아가는 바로 그 자리입니다. 우리가 일상 속에서 경험하는 작은 떨림과 깊은 몰입은 의식의 공명을 일으키며, 그 안에서 하나의 우주, 하나의 세계가 됩니다. 이번 전시는 긴 침묵과 고요 속에서 깊어지며사유한 순간들의 응축입니다. 관계로부터 단절되어 홀로 마주한 시간은 내가 지나온 길과 멈추어 선 자취이며, 동시에 또 다른 세계로의 통로입니다. 전통 서예의 맥락 위에서, 나는 고대 문자—특히 갑골문자가 지닌 원초적 형상과 기운을 불러내어, 한글의 조형적 가능성과 함께 현대의 감각으로 재구성합니다. 문자들은 단순한 소통의 도구를 넘어, 존재의 흔적이자 시각적 조형물로 드러납니다. 심장을 가진 생명처럼 호흡하는 글자는 획마다 맥박을 새기며 시간을 관통하는 궤적을 남깁니다. 「이, 별에 서서」는 특정한 별을 지칭하지 않습니다. 그것은 내가 서 있는 ‘이 자리’이며,지금-여기의 순간들입니다. 그 자리에서 피어난 문자들은 개인의 기록을 넘어, 인간이 세계를 인식하고 감각하는 방식에 대한 탐구입니다. 이 전시가 관람자에게는 또 다른 별이자, 자신의 내면을 향한 통로가 되기를 바랍니다. 그 길 위에서 단절된 관계조차 두려움 없이 수용하며, 자아로서의 빛나는 존재로 서기를 그려봅니다.

We introduce the exhibition <Happy Holidays>, which captures the temperature of the year end season. Warm crafts placed throughout the space, bonsai expressing the colors of the season, soft textures and sparkling decorations, and the witty scenes created by the illustrator Drawingdaum. Cheerful and pleasant energy fills the space like selecting a gift box. May the end of this year be a little warmer and a little more sparkling. Atelier Aechae’s winter story welcomes you. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year.
desc_l10n.ja: .se-contents .se-scrollbox{overflow-x: auto; -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none;}.se-contents .se-scrollbox::-webkit-scrollbar{display: none;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image .se-caption{max-width: 100% !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video{max-width: 100%; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-image > img, .se-contents .se-responsive.se-video > *{max-width: 100%; min-width: 10px; height: auto !important;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper{position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; display: block;}.se-contents .se-responsive.se-video .se-video-wrapper > iframe{width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important; position: absolute; left: 0px} 一年の終わりに訪れるときめき、浮き立った空気、そして少しはゆっくりと過ごしたい気持ち。 そんな年末の温度を盛り込んだ展示<Happy Holidays>をご紹介します。あちこちに置かれた温かい工芸品と季節の色味を含んだ盆栽、ふんわりとしたテクスチャーときらめく装飾、そしてイラスト作家のドローイングダウムが作り出した機知に富んだ場面まで。プレゼントボックスを選ぶように、心地よい軽快なエネルギーが空間を満たします。今年の最後がもう少し温かく、もう少し輝きますように。エチェの冬物語が皆さんをお迎えします。Merry Christmas and Happy New Year!
desc_l10n.ko: 한 해에 끝에 찾아오는 설렘, 들뜬 공기, 그리고 조금은 천천히 머물고 싶은 마음. 그런 연말의 온도를 담은 전시 <Happy Holidays>를 소개합니다. 곳곳에 놓인 따뜻한 공예품과 계절의 색감을 머금은 분재, 포근한 텍스처와 반짝이는 장식들, 그리고 일러스트 작가 드로잉다움이 만들어낸 재치 있는 장면들까지. 선물 상자를 고르듯 기분 좋은 경쾌한 에너지가 공간을 채웁니다. 올해의 마지막이 조금 더 따뜻하고, 조금 더 반짝이기를. 애채의 겨울 이야기가 여러분을 맞이합니다. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year!
